narr: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
ev: Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in a dry wash leading into Sulphur Creek from upstream heavy rainfall. The water level on Sulphur Creek near the Visitor center rose 2 feet.
Nine homes were damaged from flooding and debris flows due to heavy rain in the Enoch and Summit areas.

Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding occurred on Calf Creek, with significant debris washed over the waterfalls. Flash flooding was also reported on Egypt Road and in the Egypt slot canyons along Hole-In-The-Rock Road.

Flash flooding near Lund derailed a Union Pacific Railroad train, forcing 14 cars off of the tracks. Train tracks were determined to be washed out at a small bridge crossing over a normally dry wash. After the train derailed, injured train operators were trapped on top of the overturned train as flood waters continued to rise. In addition, emergency responders were washed off of the road to the crash site by the flood waters, delaying response to the injured train operators.
The North Fork of the Virgin River jumped to 180 CFS, a rise of 1.5 feet, after heavy rainfall over the headwaters overnight.
Kodachrome Basin State Park officials reported brief flash flooding of washes within the Park, including at the campground at the north end of the park.

Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported flash flooding on Harris Wash. The flooding occurred later as peak flow worked around from Alvy Wash into Harris Wash. Also, the Escalante River gauge near Escalante indicated a 702 CFS flood wave, with a time above 300 CFS from 1845 MDT to 2015 MDT.
